title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention with timeouts
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: - Improve continuous batcher fairness and prevent starvation by adding per-priority queue timeouts and adaptive dequeue heuristics. No API changes.
description: Motivation: production workloads showed long-tail latency regressions where low-priority/large requests starved or queue-jumped mid-batch causing throughput variance. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and add configurable per-priority timeouts so requests don't wait indefinitely. Design: introduce a dual-queue model (priority + aging queue) with adaptive dequeue weights, per-request enqueue timestamps, and a soft timeout that forces eviction to an expedited path after configurable wait thresholds. Add a token-based dequeue budget to avoid head-of-line blocking from very large requests. Implementation: changes in scheduler.py implement the enqueue/dequeue heuristics and timeout driver, queueing.py adds per-priority timeout configs and metrics hooks, and metrics_registry.go exposes new SLO metrics (queue_wait_seconds_{p0,p1,p2}, forced_evictions_total). Tests: unit tests for ordering and eviction, integration test on the perf-canary infra, and a small end-to-end scenario validating stable throughput with mixed short/long requests. Backwards compatibility: all behavior is guarded behind a feature-flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 and defaults to previous behavior. Rollout plan: enable on perf-canary, monitor queue_wait_seconds and p50/p95 token latency, then progressively roll to staged hosts. See linked Linear items for rollout approval steps.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2025-11-24): Can you justify the default timeout values? Suggest making them cluster-config overridable and adding a note about how this interacts with dedicated capacity autoscaling.

Priya Nair (2025-11-24): Default values chosen after perf-canary runs (200ms for p0, 500ms for p1, 2s for p2). Made them cluster-config overridable and added documentation section on interaction with autoscaler.

Hannah Park (2025-11-26): LGTM but please add metrics for forced evictions and a perf test showing no throughput regression at 95th percentile; also add a small safety net to avoid tearing down very large batches immediately.
Priya Nair (2025-11-27): Added forced_evictions_total metric and adjusted soft-eviction to use token budget; included perf-canary benchmark results in PR description and docs.
Ethan Zhao (2025-12-01): Approved after verifying integration test and canary dashboards. Commented that KB cache flakiness was investigated separately.
Release Manager (2025-12-02): Verified release notes and rollout plan; approved merge to main via squash.
merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash. Rollout started on perf-canary and staged hosts. No customer-facing API changes. Monitoring dashboards created for queue_wait_seconds and forced_evictions_total.
notes: Feature flag: continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 (default off for older clusters)
Config knobs: scheduler.timeout_ms.p0, scheduler.timeout_ms.p1, scheduler.timeout_ms.p2, scheduler.token_dequeue_budget
Perf results: canary run with mixed workload (70% short, 30% long) showed p95 token latency reduced by 12% and stable throughput across 2h test window
Follow-ups: add automatic knob suggestions in Redwood Optimize based on observed queue_wait_seconds distributions (ENG-4198)
Docs: docs/perf/continuous-batcher.md updated with tuning guidance and example configs
